title: Mathematical content of "isospin": the Z/2 grading of any Frobenius spin involution
html:
Remark. Isospin is the \mathbb{Z}/2 grading attached to any Frobenius algebra equipped with a spin involution; nucleons are one instance. When physical observables are extracted as \tau-traces of products of central elements and braid recipes, the spin-singlet sector and spin-doublet sector decompose canonically under the LP-dual. The Wigner energy term \sim |Z - N|/A in the BW formula is the T_3-projection of this grading. It appears because |Z - N| is the \mathbb{Z}/2 charge of the recipe, which the LP-dual reads off mechanically.

The proof does not invoke Lie theory or SU(2) symmetries. Any quantum-algebraic system with a trace-preserving spin involution, a \sigma-invariant central cost, and a \sigma-stable channel set inherits LP-dual spin-invariance. Particle physics exhibits isospin because nucleons populate a 2-row Wedderburn stratum governed by the same algebra.
